sheet-1-1.description: The lower left of Sheet 1, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, shows the east end of Belvidere's Water Street where it leaves the town grid at Adams Street and curves north-east towards the Pequest Creek. Adams Street runs down the left edge and Water Street crosses the part near the top, with six and eight inch water pipes and hydrants drawn in it. North of Water Street stand the American Piano Hammer Co. works, a concrete-floored factory with automatic sprinklers and a stone and leather storehouse, and Capitol Park, an amusement ground with a dance hall, a shooting gallery, booths and a carousel outline. South of Water Street, in blocks 6 and 7, are frame dwellings along Adams Street, two private alleys running east from it, a driveway, and the large Roseberry Bros. garage and storage building with an office and supply room, whose note gives capacity for 65 cars. The Pequest Creek crosses the lower right corner, with vacant ground beside it. The scale of feet is printed at the bottom left. The part is bounded by heavy lines: above it is the key map of the town and to its right the Riverton, Pa. part of the same sheet. The north arrow printed on this part points straight up the page, but the street grid here is turned about ten degrees from it, as on the adjoining Sheet 4, which draws the west side of Adams Street.
notes: Placed from the single junction Adams Street / Water Street, with the rotation of its measured lines and the atlas scale (anchored; low confidence).
The printed north arrow points straight up, about 10 degrees from the fitted north; the fitted rotation agrees with Sheet 4.

Upper half: key map of Belvidere at 500 ft (not a part), index and water/fire notes. Lower half at 50 ft: part 1 Water Street and Adams Street (blocks 6, 7, American Piano Hammer Co, Capitol Park, Roseberry Bros garage); part 2 Riverton, Pa. (blocks 225-227, Public Road, Bridge Street, Alpha Portland Cement Co farm), turned about 45 degrees. Printed north arrows on this atlas read about 10 degrees low (part 1 fits at 9.85 degrees with its arrow straight up).

sheet-1-2.description: The lower right of Sheet 1, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, shows Riverton, Pennsylvania, on the west bank of the Delaware River opposite Belvidere, "located 1/4 mile from fire house at Belvidere", with no water works, no fire department and electric lights. The part is turned on the page: its own north arrow points to the upper right. Public Road runs up the part from the river crossing, and Bridge Street (marked arbitrary) runs from it to the steel toll bridge, 642 ft long, whose Pennsylvania end is drawn at the right edge where the bridge meets the river bank. Blocks 225, 226 and 227 are numbered. Buildings are few: a hotel and the Riverton Hotel (heated by stoves, lit by kerosene oil) near the bridge, dwellings with barns along Bridge Street, a lane and a driveway, a corn crib, and at the bottom the farm buildings of the Alpha Portland Cement Co., owners, with a barn, a wagon house, a cistern and a farm house. Vacant fields fill much of the lower half. The Delaware River and an island are drawn along the right side.
notes: Riverton is in Pennsylvania, outside the statewide reference data; the two control points (Public Road / Bridge Street, modern Riverton Road / Martins Creek Belvidere Highway, and the Pennsylvania end of the Riverton-Belvidere Bridge) were taken from OpenStreetMap separately.
Placed from one point with the atlas scale and north set to 43 degrees (the printed arrow, about 34 degrees, read 10 degrees low as on Sheet 1 part 1); low confidence.

(blocks 225-227, Public Road, Bridge Street, Alpha Portland Cement Co farm), turned about 45 degrees. Printed north arrows on this atlas read about 10 degrees low (part 1 fits at 9.85 degrees with its arrow straight up).

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, covers the west side of Belvidere's business district between the Pequest Creek and the Delaware River approach. Water Street crosses the top of the sheet, with Wall Street marked only by its water pipe; the Pequest Creek, its islands and the head race run across the upper half, with South Water Street along the creek's south bank. Front Street crosses the middle of the sheet and 2nd Street the bottom, both running slightly uphill to the right on the page, and Depue Street runs down the left side. Greenwich Street forms the right edge, with Market Street at the top right corner. The tracks of the Pennsylvania Railroad's Belvidere Delaware line run down the middle of the sheet past the passenger station, freight station and Depot Park. Industry lines the water: the S. W. Gardner & Co. saw and planing mill and lumber yard, the Belvidere Flouring Mills on the head race and tail race, the L. E. Ritter lumber yard with long lumber sheds, and the S. H. Dayton coal yard. Agricultural implement and wire fence warehouses and a hardware store stand on Water Street near Market Street. The rest of the sheet holds frame dwellings on long narrow lots along Front Street and Depue Street, a private alley and driveways.
notes: Wall Street is drawn only as a water pipe at the top of the sheet; its junction with Water Street was not used.
50 ft. Front, Water, Depue, Greenwich, 2nd Street, Pequest Creek, railroad (Pennsylvania R.R.).

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, covers the centre of Belvidere between Water Street at the top and 2nd Street at the bottom, Greenwich and Market Streets on the left and Hardwick and Prospect Streets on the right. The Pequest Creek and a head race cross the upper part of the sheet, with the Warren Wood Working Co. (formerly a mill, with water wheel and electric plant) on the creek at Market Street, and a mill construction factory building and the Buser Co. silk ribbon mill on the south bank by Prospect Street. Mill Street runs diagonally from the Market Street bridge to Front Street, with Standish Place off it. Front Street is the business street: the Belvidere National Bank, the Masonic Temple, the J. A. Jackson & Co. department store, the Warren County Trust Co., stores, a hotel, a printing office and the Hotel Belvidere at the corner of Hardwick Street. Mansfield Street runs down the middle of the sheet from Front Street to 2nd Street, past a public library; on the block between Mansfield and Hardwick Streets near 2nd Street stand the county buildings and the jail. Along Water Street are Widenor's hall with a theatre, a fire department building, the town hall and dwellings. Water pipes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are drawn in the streets, and the scale of feet is printed at the bottom.
notes: Front Street / Greenwich Street was detected 7 m from the fit and left out.
50 ft. Downtown: Water, Market, Prospect, Mill, Front, Greenwich, Mansfield, Hardwick, 2nd Street, Pequest Creek; pilot sheet.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, covers the east side of Belvidere between Prospect Street on the left and Adams Street on the right. Water Street crosses the upper part of the sheet, with Washington Street running north from it; above Water Street are blocks 4 and 5 of frame dwellings with an unnamed street along the top and no exposure beyond. South of Water Street, block 9 and block 8 hold more dwellings and the Washington Felting Co. mill, makers of piano hammer felts. The lower half is taken by water: the Pequest Creek crosses the sheet diagonally, the head race of the Dolphin Mills runs below it, and the Mill Pond fills the bottom right. At the lower left, on Hardwick Street, stand the Dolphin Mills of George R. McMurtrie, a flour mill built in 1876, with grain bins, an engine house and a water wheel, and the Crane Felt Co. piano felt works beside the creek. Oxford Street leaves Hardwick Street at the bottom left with dwellings along it, and Race Street is marked at the bottom right. Driveways cross the open ground between the creek and the head race. The north arrow is printed beside the Mill Pond and the scale of feet at the bottom.
notes: The unnamed street at the top of the sheet was tried as modern Vanatta Place and left out: it pulled the fit by several metres.
50 ft. Water, Washington, Adams streets, Pequest Creek and Mill Pond.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, is turned on the page: north points to the right, so Hardwick Street runs along the top of the sheet and Knowlton Street across its middle, while 3rd Street and 2nd Street run up and down the page. It covers the south-east side of Belvidere around the Mill Pond. The upper left holds blocks of frame dwellings between Hardwick, Knowlton, 2nd and 3rd Streets, with the M. E. Church on Hardwick Street and the Presbyterian Home for the Aged near the top right corner. Oxford Street crosses the lower half diagonally from the bottom left towards the upper right, lined with small dwellings on narrow lots, and Race Street runs beside it to the right, along the Mill Pond, which is drawn at the right edge. Parker Street crosses the bottom of the sheet with more dwellings. Block numbers 26, 105, 104, 106, 231 and 208 are printed, with water pipes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes in the streets. The lower left corner is vacant field, and the scale of feet is printed there. A compass rose stands in the block between 3rd Street and Knowlton Street.
notes: The sheet is turned 90 degrees: north points to the right of the page.
50 ft. Hardwick, Knowlton, Oxford, Race, Parker streets and the public park.

sheet-6-1.description: The main part of Sheet 6, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers the north side of Belvidere from Water Street at the bottom to beyond Delaware Avenue at the top, and from the Delaware River bank on the left to Prospect Street on the right. Wall Street and Market Street run up the sheet; Paul Street (West Paul west of Wall Street), James Street, Wurts Street and Delaware Avenue cross it, with Green Lane leaving Market Street opposite Paul Street. The railroad (P.R.R., Belvidere Delaware line) curves through the middle of the sheet from the bottom towards the upper right, where Back Road runs beside it, and a branch runs west along block 202. Most of the sheet is frame dwellings on deep lots. Below Paul Street the large block 2 is mostly open ground with a few buildings; along Water Street at the bottom a row of stores and dwellings faces the street. On Market Street near Green Lane are the 2nd Presbyterian Church and its parsonage, and a steep, rocky bluff runs across block 3 towards Prospect Street. Fish Street (marked arbitrary) and a private alley run off Wall Street on the left. Two insets occupy the top left of the sheet and are separate parts. The scale of 100 ft to one inch is printed at the bottom right.
notes: Wurts Street is spelled Wurtz Street in OpenStreetMap.
Back Road is taken to be modern Manunkachunk Road.
Fish Street (arbitrary) is modern Fisk Street.

100 ft. Part 1 north Belvidere (Wall, Market, Paul, James, Wurts, Delaware Av, Back Rd, Water, Prospect, Green Lane); part 2 inset W. Paul at the Delaware River (Sunbury Converting Works); part 3 inset Hazen, 2 miles east (Belvidere Main Rd).

sheet-6-2.description: Part 2 of Sheet 6 is an inset in the top left corner of the sheet, drawn at 100 ft to an inch with its own north arrow. It continues the main part to the west: West Paul Street runs from the right edge to the bank of the Delaware River, which crosses the left side of the inset. At the river end of West Paul Street stand the Sunbury Converting Works, formerly the Belvidere Water Co. pumping station, with a pump house, a wood and steel truss building with a concrete floor, a coal shed and a suction pipe running into the river, and an engineer's house nearby. East of it is the Riverside Poultry Yard of M. P. Frome, with feed houses and a long poultry house, which is also drawn at the left edge of the main part. A driveway runs down the slope along the top of the steep river bank, and a few small buildings stand near the bottom of the inset. Block numbers 32 and 1 are printed north and south of West Paul Street. An eight inch water pipe, marked not in use, runs along the street.
notes: Placed from two points carried from part 1 (West Paul Street and the east end of the long poultry house drawn on both parts), with the scale and rotation of part 1; low confidence.

100 ft. Part 1 north Belvidere (Wall, Market, Paul, James, Wurts, Delaware Av, Back Rd, Water, Prospect, Green Lane); part 2 inset W. Paul at the Delaware River (Sunbury Converting Works); part 3 inset Hazen, 2 miles east (Belvidere Main Rd).

sheet-6-3.description: Part 3 of Sheet 6 is an inset at the top of the sheet showing the hamlet of Hazen, "located 2 miles east of fire house at Belvidere", population 100, with no water facilities and no fire department and kerosene lights. It is drawn at 100 ft to an inch with its own north arrow. Belvidere Main Road crosses the inset from left to right, marked as the road to Belvidere at the left and 3 miles to Oxford at the right; it crosses Bulgens Brook on a stone arch bridge. A road marked 7 miles to Washington leaves the main road beside the brook and runs down the inset. Blocks 101 and 102 are numbered. North of the road stand a few dwellings, a barn, a hay loft, a wagon house and fowl houses; south of it are a store, dwellings, a wood shed, an ice house, sheds, a smoke house and a wagon shed. The inset is bordered by no exposure on the north, east and south and woods beyond on the south-west.
notes: Belvidere Main Road is today Brass Castle Road (towards Belvidere) and Hazen - Oxford Road (towards Oxford); the road to Washington is Brass Castle Road south of the junction.

Placed from the single junction of the Washington road with Belvidere Main Road (modern Brass Castle Road / Hazen - Oxford Road), with the nominal scale and the rotation of its measured lines; low confidence.

100 ft. Part 1 north Belvidere (Wall, Market, Paul, James, Wurts, Delaware Av, Back Rd, Water, Prospect, Green Lane); part 2 inset W. Paul at the Delaware River (Sunbury Converting Works); part 3 inset Hazen, 2 miles east (Belvidere Main Rd).

sheet-7-1.description: The main part of Sheet 7, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, covers the south side of Belvidere from 2nd Street at the top to 7th Street at the bottom, and from the Delaware River on the left to Hardwick Street and Independence Street on the right. Depue Street runs along the river at the upper left, Spring, Greenwich, Mansfield and Hardwick Streets run down the sheet, and 2nd to 7th Streets cross it. The tracks of the Pennsylvania Railroad and the Lehigh and Hudson River Railroad sweep through the left side, past the L. E. Ritter coal yard, the Waddington Condensed Milk Co. and a bridge at 4th Street; the Pophandusing Creek winds from the river across the lower left. Public buildings include the Presbyterian church and Sunday school on 2nd Street, the public park filling the block at the top right, the Belvidere Public School, St. Patrick's R. C. Church, the Zion Episcopal Church and a second public school on Mansfield Street. Frank M. Bair's garage stands on Mansfield Street, and the John Dalrymple saw mill (not in operation) and the Belford & Niedermiller coal yard lie by the creek near 6th Street. Most blocks hold frame dwellings; those south of 5th Street are largely vacant lots. Two insets at the bottom left are separate parts.
notes: 100 ft. Part 1 south Belvidere (Depue, Spring, Greenwich, Mansfield, Hardwick, 2nd to 7th Streets, Pophandusing Creek, railroads); part 2 inset block 31A on the Delaware River (continues part 1 to the west, match line A-B); part 3 inset south of 7th Street between Mansfield and Hardwick Streets (block 230).

sheet-7-2.description: Part 2 of Sheet 7 is an inset at the bottom left of the sheet, drawn at 100 ft to an inch with its own north arrow. It continues the main part directly to the west: a dash-dot match line lettered A and B at its ends is drawn on both, and the four tracks of the Pennsylvania Railroad cross it on both. The inset shows the east bank of the Delaware River with block 31A, where an old vacant building and a few dwellings stand near the river. The railroad crosses the inset diagonally, and a road or fence line runs beside it towards the match line. The rest of the inset is open ground.
notes: Placed from two points carried from part 1 along the match line A-B, where the railroad crosses it on both parts, with the scale and rotation of part 1; low confidence.

100 ft. Part 1 south Belvidere (Depue, Spring, Greenwich, Mansfield, Hardwick, 2nd to 7th Streets, Pophandusing Creek, railroads); part 2 inset block 31A on the Delaware River (continues part 1 to the west, match line A-B); part 3 inset south of 7th Street between Mansfield and Hardwick Streets (block 230).

sheet-7-3.description: Part 3 of Sheet 7 is an inset at the bottom of the sheet, drawn at 100 ft to an inch, bounded by heavy lines. It shows the ground south of 7th Street between Mansfield Street and Hardwick Street, block 230. 7th Street crosses the top of the inset; Mansfield Street runs diagonally down from it across the Pophandusing Creek and the tracks of the Lehigh and Hudson River Railroad; Hardwick Street is marked at the top right corner with a ten inch water pipe. Beside the tracks stand the railroad depot and a platform, a railroad water tank and a tool house; a long coal shed or siding building stands at the left edge. Two dwellings face Mansfield Street north of the creek. The compass rose of the sheet is printed at the top of the inset, and the scale bar is at its right.
notes: Placed from the single junction 7th Street / Mansfield Street, with the nominal scale and the rotation of its measured lines; low confidence. Its Hardwick Street is drawn about 10 percent closer to Mansfield Street than on part 1.

100 ft. Part 1 south Belvidere (Depue, Spring, Greenwich, Mansfield, Hardwick, 2nd to 7th Streets, Pophandusing Creek, railroads); part 2 inset block 31A on the Delaware River (continues part 1 to the west, match line A-B); part 3 inset south of 7th Street between Mansfield and Hardwick Streets (block 230).

sheet-8-1.description: The main part of Sheet 8, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, shows the village of Delaware, N.J., "located 6 miles north of Belvidere", population 300, with no hydrants and no fire department. Public Road runs up the left side; beside it the two railroads, the L. R.R. and the N.Y.S.& W. R.R., run up the sheet past the passenger and freight stations, and Railroad street runs along their east side. Charles Street and Clinton Street cross the village between Railroad street and Valley street, which runs down the sheet and bends to the north-east at the top. Prall Avenue runs north from Charles Street. Block 105 between Charles and Clinton Streets is the village centre: a livery, an agricultural implement store, the Lackawanna House, a flour and feed store, a monument and stone cutting works, and a building with a store and the post office. The Delaware Creamery stands by the tracks at the bottom left. Dwellings stand along Charles, Clinton and Prall Avenue and up Valley street, where a lane, a cistern fed by a brook and the M. W. Ammerman shop lie at the top. Streets marked not opened cross the bottom of the sheet. The strip at the top left and the part to the right of the heavy line are separate parts.
notes: Valley is today Delaware Road north of Clinton Street and Valley Street south of it.

Placed from one point (Public Road at the crossing road, modern US 46 / Clinton Street / Roy Ace Street) with north set to 27 degrees so that Public Road and the railroads follow modern US 46 and the former DL&W line; a second junction (Clinton / Valley) gave 17 degrees and was left out. Low confidence.

50 ft. Delaware, N.J., 6 miles north of Belvidere. Part 1 Public Road, Railroad, Charles, Clinton, Prall Av, Valley (modern US 46, Clinton Street, Delaware Road / Valley Street); part 2 top-left strip of Public Road north of the village (blocks 250, 251; not placed); part 3 strip continuing Valley southwards (Aurelia, Ferry = modern Clarence Road), drawn to the right of a heavy line.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: strip of Public Road and the two railroads north of the village (blocks 250, 251, John H. Hoyt Company storage) (no street junction; notes give only distances (750 ft to dwelling 207 Prall Av); needs parcel corners or a building matched on an aerial along US 46 north of Delaware).

sheet-8-3.description: Part 3 of Sheet 8, drawn at 50 ft to an inch, is set off by heavy lines on the right of the sheet and continues the village of Delaware southwards along Valley street: the street marked not opened and the sheet number at its top match those at the bottom of the main part. Valley runs down the right side of the part with the steep mountain side and woods beyond it. Aurelia Street, marked not opened, and Ferry Street cross the part, with blocks 104, 106 and 218. Buildings are dwellings with barns and sheds, the St. James Episcopal Church, the Presbyterian parsonage, the Presbyterian Church at the corner of Ferry Street and Valley, and the Quig Bros. garage at the bottom right corner. Notes give distances to the railroad tracks to the west. The compass rose of the sheet and the scale of feet are printed along its left edge.
notes: Ferry Street is today Clarence Road east of US 46 (Ferry Lane west of it).

Placed from the single junction Ferry / Valley (modern Clarence Road / Valley Street) with the atlas scale and the rotation of its measured lines; low confidence. Its top lines up with the bottom of part 1.
